messages:
jess: hey @mike, saw your support ticket about billing spikes after a bunch of 429s. can you drop a short timeline and any logs you have?
mike_customer: sure. started around 2026-03-15 09:00 UTC. our app got a cluster of 429 responses, then our retry wrapper replayed and we ended up with duplicate orders and extra billing. running node SDK v1.2.0.
jess: do you set an Idempotency-Key header for order creation calls?
mike_customer: we do not. we have an internal retry helper that wraps fetch. logs look like this (truncated):
```
[2026-03-15T08:59:58Z] POST /v1/orders -> 429 (X-Request-Id: rQ7d2)
[2026-03-15T08:59:58Z] retry #1 -> POST /v1/orders -> 200 (order_id: ord_123)
[2026-03-15T08:59:58Z] retry #2 -> POST /v1/orders -> 200 (order_id: ord_124)
```
mike_customer: two distinct order ids returned on retries. seems like the server created twice because the retried requests did not include idempotency.
jess: can you re-run with verbose headers (capture X-Request-Id, any X-Rate-Limit-*, Retry-After)? that'll help. also paste exact SDK version string. i'll involve eng for retry guidance.

ryan_eng: looped in. quick read: this is a common pattern when clients use immediate or linear retries without idempotency. note: node SDK v1.2.0 default backoff was aggressive and deterministic (fixed increments), which leads to retry storms. server-side idempotency exists for many create endpoints but only if the Idempotency-Key header is present and dedupe window hasn't expired.

ryan_eng: short-term recommendations:
- add a client-generated Idempotency-Key (UUID per logical op) on create POSTs
- switch retries to exponential backoff with full jitter
- honor Retry-After header from server when present
- instrument logs to include X-Request-Id and Idempotency-Key so support/eng can trace duplicates

tanvi_sre: SRE notes: when a key hits burst quota, the rate limiter may emit 429s without Retry-After during transient bursts. clients that retry synchronously just amplify the burst. prefer randomized exponential backoff. also check if you're behind a proxy/CDN that may also retry on connect failures (double retry problem).

ryan_eng: safe retry pseudocode (full jitter):
```
base = 0.1  # seconds
cap = 5.0   # seconds
attempt = 0
while attempt < max_attempts:
  wait = random.uniform(0, min(cap, base * 2**attempt))
  sleep(wait)
  resp = send(request)
  if resp.status in [200,201,202]: return resp
  if resp.status == 429:
    if 'Retry-After' in resp.headers:
      sleep(float(resp.headers['Retry-After']))
  attempt += 1
```

mike_customer: couple questions:
- does the API dedupe every create if Idempotency-Key is present, or are there endpoints that ignore it?
- should we remove our custom retry wrapper and rely solely on the SDK's retry logic? we added the wrapper to handle transient network blips.

ryan_eng: server honors Idempotency-Key for most POST/create endpoints, but there are edge cases (e.g., streaming or long-poll flows) where it's not applied. best practice: keep a client-generated idempotency key and keep retries, but adopt the exponential+jitter strategy. SDK v1.3.0 will auto-generate idempotency for supported endpoints and uses exponential backoff by default — upgrading helps.

jess: next steps for support:
- run a repro with verbose headers enabled (capture X-Request-Id and any X-Rate-Limit- headers, Retry-After)
- try adding Idempotency-Key and confirm single-create behavior
- if possible, test with SDK v1.3.0 in staging to see improved defaults

mike_customer: i'll run tests and attach curl output. sample curl i'm going to use:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount":100, "customer":"cus_abc"}'
```

tanvi_sre: also validate whether any upstream proxy is adding retries. if you're behind a managed load balancer, check its retry policy. that often explains duplicates even when client code looks fine.

ryan_eng: if after adding idempotency + exponential+jitter you still see duplicates, reply here and i'll open an eng-runtime investigation. include: X-Request-Id values for the duplicate traces, exact SDK version, and redacted raw headers/bodies.

jess: thanks everyone. @mike once you paste the repro logs we'll triage further. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: FYI scheduled maintenance: rate-limiter tuning 2026-03-17T02:00:00Z

mike_customer: thanks all, running the repro now; will post results in this thread when done :pray:
